question.text: Mr. Vikram Joshi is the sponsor of 'Saraswati Growth Fund', a Cat II AIF with a target corpus of INR 400 crore. What is the MINIMUM continuing sponsor/manager 'skin-in-the-game' commitment he must maintain under Regulation 10(d)?

answer.text: INR 4 crore or 1% of corpus, whichever is lower
INR 5 crore or 2.5% of corpus, whichever is lower
INR 10 crore or 5% of corpus, whichever is lower
INR 20 crore or 10% of corpus, whichever is lower

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 10(d) SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012: for Cat I and Cat II AIFs, the sponsor / manager must maintain continuing interest of at least 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is LOWER. On INR 400 crore corpus, 2.5% = INR 10 crore; INR 5 crore is the lower figure and is the binding floor. The Trap: The '5% or INR 10 crore' option is the Cat III rule - a classic swap. 1% understates. 10% is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests both Cat I/II and Cat III versions side by side. XIX-E (future) will focus on Cat III 5% rule. XXI-B has no analogous rule for PMS. Manager's Pro-Tip: Sponsor skin is drawn down pari-passu with LP calls. Don't pre-fund it - a 'true-up' at each drawdown keeps sponsor and LP economics aligned.
